svg.title: JSON, Protobuf, FIX TagValue, and SBE compared
svg.desc: An illustrative order has identifier 7, quantity 100, and price 123.45. JSON sends field names. Protobuf sends binary field keys and values, decoded with a schema. FIX TagValue uses a trading dictionary and numbered textual fields. SBE uses a template header and binary values at schema-defined positions in its fixed block. These are teaching examples, not complete broker messages or a message-size benchmark.

g.text: One small order sketch, four representations
ID 7, quantity 100, price $123.45; toy tick size = $0.01
JSON: names and values in readable text
Protobuf: numbered fields and binary values
FIX TagValue: trading tags and textual values
SBE: a template and a predictable binary layout
{"id":7,"qty":100,"priceTicks":12345}
The receiver reads field names and parses their values.
Easy to inspect; the API still defines types, units, and required fields.
The schema maps field numbers 1, 2, 3 to ID, quantity, and price ticks.
Seven bytes here, excluding framing and other request data; not self-describing.
35=D: new order; 11: client ID; 38: quantity; 44: price.
Incomplete fragment. Pipes stand for SOH delimiters; a real order needs more fields.
Template / schema header
Describes how to decode
ID: 7
uint32
Qty: 100
uint32
Price ticks: 12345
int64
Toy root-block offsets: ID at 0, quantity at 4, price ticks at 8.
16-byte fixed block plus header; groups and variable data need more structure.
Conceptual illustrations, not IBKR schemas or production-ready orders.
Panels are not drawn to byte scale. Binary does not always mean fewer bytes.
